scores.evidence: Foundation: versioned catalog, flat and per-seat subscriptions, cards, invoices, basic dunning, the tax adapter, entitlements, and the ledger. Adding a ledger later is painful.
scores.rationale: Phasing is roughly substrate-first (ledger early, usage then enterprise then global), but Phase 1 is bundled and nothing is gated on proof of the prior layer.

scores.evidence: Foundation: versioned catalog, flat and per-seat subscriptions, cards, invoices, basic dunning, the tax adapter, entitlements, and the ledger.
scores.rationale: Phase 1 is an end-to-end billing slice, but it is a broad feature bundle rather than a thin production walking skeleton.

scores.evidence: Shard by the top-level `customer_id`... Design keys for sharding from day one, but only shard (Citus, by `customer_id`) when you need to.
scores.rationale: Many decisions carry defaults and some triggers (build vs buy, sharding, numbering), but there is no consolidated up-front gate list with flip conditions.
Nothing orders work within phases by blast radius; phases are flat feature lists.

scores.evidence: The gateway maps each token to a `customer_id`, and every database transaction runs `SET LOCAL app.customer_id`. RLS then hides all other customers' rows
scores.rationale: Security is detailed (RLS, PCI, KMS, approvals), but it sits in standalone sections and is not tied to each phase.

scores.evidence: Business-level alerts: billing-run delay, drafts stuck > 2 h, payment success rate, reconciliation mismatches
scores.rationale: Alerts and reconciliation are described, but only in a standalone table, not as Phase 0 and per-phase deliverables.

scores.evidence: Build simulated clocks per customer from day one. That's the only practical way to test a three-year contract with price steps.
scores.rationale: Reproducibility exists in recomputable invoices, snapshots, and parallel-run migration, but there is no environment or build reproducibility threaded through the phases.

scores.evidence: Every operation is safe to repeat. That covers API writes, usage events, scheduled jobs, payment-provider calls, and webhook handlers.
scores.rationale: Resilience is strong in design (idempotency, outbox, fail-open, reconciliation), but it is a cross-cutting section and not stated per phase.
The plan never says whether an AI layer applies (the llm.tokens example is only a metered event type), so there is no explicit N/A declaration.

scores.evidence: Global: regional cells, the silo tier, e-invoicing channels, testing pricing changes against past usage.
scores.rationale: Later phases show what is deferred, but the plan gives no pull-forward conditions.

note: The plan is a strong technical reference architecture, but it is weak on phase-level process: there is no Phase 0 skeleton, no blast-radius ordering, no per-phase threading, no pull-forward triggers, and no AI N/A declaration.
